name: Amar Opening: Paris Gambit
description: White plays an unconventional knight to h3 and fianchetto-like pawn advances, then gambles with f4 to grab kingside space.

name: Amar Opening: Paris Gambit, Gent Gambit
description: Black captures the misplaced h3 knight and accepts multiple pawns on f4 and g3, exploiting White's weak kingside structure.

name: Anderssen's Opening: Polish Gambit
description: Both sides advance queenside pawns, with White pushing a3 and b4 in a rare flank-based opening strategy.

name: Barnes Opening: Fool's Mate
description: White fatally weakens the kingside with f3 and g4, allowing Black's queen to deliver immediate checkmate on h4.

name: Barnes Opening: Gedult Gambit
description: White weakens f3, then sacrifices the central e-pawn to Black while developing Nc3 for counterplay.

name: Barnes Opening: Hammerschlag
description: White plays the bizarre f3 followed by the dangerous king move Kf2, abandoning safety for unclear attacking ideas.

name: Clemenz Opening: Spike Lee Gambit
description: Both sides push h-pawns in an irregular opening, then White seizes kingside space with g4.

name: Creepy Crawly Formation: Classical Defense
description: White maneuvers with flank pawns h3 and a3, while Black seizes central space with d5 and e5.

name: Formation: Hippopotamus Attack
description: White methodically advances all pawns in a solid formation while Black develops normally with pieces and castles.

name: Formation: Shy Attack
description: White builds a fianchettoed position with Bg2 and careful pawn structure as Black occupies the center and develops.

name: Grob Opening: Alessi Gambit
description: White advances g4 to seize kingside space, but Black immediately counters the kingside thrust with f5.

name: Grob Opening: Double Grob
description: Both sides push g-pawns toward each other, creating a unique doubled pawn structure on the kingside.

name: Grob Opening: Double Grob, Coca-Cola Gambit
description: After g4 and g5, White sacrifices further kingside pawns with f4, offering wild tactical complications.

name: Grob Opening: Grob Gambit
description: White sacrifices the g-pawn and fianchettoes the bishop, allowing Black central expansion with d5.

name: Grob Opening: Grob Gambit, Basman Gambit
description: Black attacks White's g-pawn with h5, and White captures, opening the h-file for tactical play.

name: Grob Opening: Grob Gambit Declined
description: Black declines the g-pawn, instead solidifying the center with d5 and c6 for a solid setup.

name: Grob Opening: Grob Gambit, Fritz Gambit
description: White fianchettoes, Black captures on the kingside, and White strikes the center with c4.

name: Grob Opening: Grob Gambit, Fritz Gambit, Romford Countergambit
description: Both sides sacrifice material furiously: White's bishop invades the queenside while Black's queen recaptures from a8.

name: Grob Opening: Grob Gambit, Keres Gambit
description: White fianchettoes, then sacrifices the d-pawn with d4, supporting the center with c3.

name: Grob Opening: Grob Gambit, Richter-Grob Gambit
description: White sacrifices the c-pawn to maintain central pressure while Black supports d5 with c6.

name: Grob Opening: Keene Defense
description: White advances kingside pawns before fianchettoing, while Black establishes a solid central duo with supporting moves.

name: Grob Opening: Keene Defense, Main Line
description: White plays d4 to undermine Black's center, then c4, while Black develops the bishop and knight defensively.

name: Grob Opening: London Defense
description: White advances kingside pawns while Black seizes the center with e5 and develops the knight.

name: Grob Opening: Romford Countergambit
description: After Black captures on g4, White's c4 thrust is met by Black's d4 advance, deepening the center struggle.

name: Grob Opening: Spike Attack
description: White fianchettoes and then aggressively advances g5, attempting to open lines on the kingside.

name: Grob Opening: Spike, Hurst Attack
description: Black's dual central pawns are challenged by White's c4 thrust, creating tactical skirmishes.

name: Grob Opening: Zilbermints Gambit
description: White sacrifices the central e-pawn with e4, offering material to develop Nc3 and build attacking play.

name: Grob Opening: Zilbermints Gambit, Schiller Defense
description: Black captures the e-pawn and counterattacks White's kingside with h5, creating threats on both flanks.

name: Grob Opening: Zilbermints Gambit, Zilbermints-Hartlaub Gambit
description: Black strengthens the center with e5 while White solidifies with d3, creating a balanced pawn structure.

name: Hungarian Opening: Asten Gambit
description: White and Black clash in the center with d4 and e5, then White sacrifices the knight with Ne4 while Black advances f5.

name: Hungarian Opening: Bücker Gambit
description: White fianchettoes while Black seizes the center with d5 and e5, and White counterattacks with b4.

name: Hungarian Opening: Burk Gambit
description: Black establishes a strong pawn center, and White maneuvers the knight to h4 while supporting with d3.

name: Hungarian Opening: Catalan Formation
description: White fianchettoes while Black builds a solid structure with d5 and e6, resembling the Catalan Defense.

name: Hungarian Opening: Dutch Defense
description: White fianchettoes while Black advances the f-pawn, establishing a Dutch Defense-like kingside structure.

name: Hungarian Opening: Indian Defense
description: White fianchettoes as Black plays the flexible knight to f6, a typical Indian Defense approach.

name: Hungarian Opening: Myers Defense
description: Both sides advance the g-pawn, creating an unusual mirror structure on the kingside.

name: Hungarian Opening: Pachman Gambit
description: White sacrifices the e-pawn with e4 and launches a checking attack with Qh5, forcing Black to block on g6.

name: Hungarian Opening: Paris Gambit
description: White sacrifices the knight and f-pawn for rapid kingside attacking chances, castling to secure the king.

name: Hungarian Opening: Reversed Alekhine
description: White fianchettoes while Black expands the center; White develops the knight in a Reversed Alekhine setup.

name: Hungarian Opening: Reversed Brooklyn Defense, Brooklyn Benko Gambit
description: Black's e4 forces White's knight retreat to g1, then White counterattacks with b4 on the queenside.

name: Hungarian Opening: Reversed Modern Defense
description: White fianchettoes while Black expands with d5 and c5, controlling both the center and queenside.

name: Hungarian Opening: Reversed Norwegian Defense
description: Black's e4 advance forces the developed knight away to h4, maneuvering away from the advanced pawn.

name: Hungarian Opening: Sicilian Invitation
description: White fianchettoes while Black immediately claims the queenside with c5, inverting the typical Sicilian.

name: Hungarian Opening: Slav Formation
description: White fianchettoes as Black establishes a solid Slav-like structure with d5 and c6.

name: Hungarian Opening: Symmetrical Variation
description: Both sides advance the g-pawn, creating a perfect mirror of the fianchetto structure.

name: Hungarian Opening: Van Kuijk Gambit
description: Black aggressively advances h-pawns while White develops the knight, creating kingside complications.

name: Hungarian Opening: Winterberg Gambit
description: White sacrifices the c-pawn with c4 to maintain pressure, and after Black captures, White plays b3 to reclaim.

name: Kádas Opening: Beginner's Trap
description: White plays the unusual h4 opening, then moves the rook to h3 in a dubious, trap-prone setup.

name: Kádas Opening: Kádas Gambit
description: White opens with h4 and sacrifices the central d-pawn with d4, supporting the center with c3.

name: Kádas Opening: Koola-Koola Variation
description: White's offbeat h4 is met by Black's a5, both sides advancing flank pawns without central engagement.

name: Kádas Opening: Myers Variation
description: White opens with rare h4, meeting Black's d5 with d4 and e4 to stake a claim in the center.

name: Kádas Opening: Schneider Gambit
description: White's h4 meets Black's aggressive g5, with both sides immediately seizing space on the kingside.

name: Kádas Opening: Steinbok Gambit
description: White sacrifices the e4 pawn to open lines after Black's f5; d3 maintains central presence.

name: Mieses Opening: Myers Spike Attack
description: White plays quiet d3, then storms the kingside with g4 while maintaining a flexible setup.

name: Mieses Opening: Reversed Rat
description: White plays the quiet d3, and Black responds with central e5, both sides preparing flexible structures.

name: Mieses Opening: Venezolana Variation
description: White develops with d3 and Nc3 as Black counters with c5 and Nc6, creating balanced piece activity.

name: Polish Opening: Baltic Defense
description: White's unusual b4 setup prepares fianchetto while Black quickly seizes the center with d5 and develops the bishop to f5.

name: Polish Opening: Birmingham Gambit
description: White's unusual queenside b4 is met by Black's immediate central c5 counterattack, creating immediate imbalance.

name: Polish Opening: Bugayev Advance Variation
description: White advances the queenside pawn to b5 while Black defends e5 with f6, creating strategic tension.

name: Polish Opening: Bugayev Attack
description: After b4 and Black's e5, White consolidates with a3, preventing knight moves and keeping options open.

name: Polish Opening: Czech Defense
description: Black solidifies the center with e5 and d6, creating a solid structure against White's fianchetto.

name: Polish Opening: Dutch Defense
description: Black immediately counterattacks the kingside with f5 in response to White's unusual queenside b4 opening.

name: Polish Opening: German Defense
description: Black seizes the center with d5 and develops the queen to d6, meeting White's fianchetto setup.

name: Polish Opening: Grigorian Variation
description: Black immediately develops a knight to c6, meeting White's unusual b4 with central piece coordination.

name: Polish Opening: Karniewski Variation
description: Black develops the knight to the rim with Nh6, responding to White's unusual queenside b4.

description: Black develops in King's Indian style with Nf6 and g6, preparing fianchetto against White's queenside setup.

description: White launches e4 to break the center while Black fianchettoes with g6, creating tactical complications.

name: Polish Opening: King's Indian Variation, Sokolsky Attack
description: White builds a classical center (c4, d4, e3) while Black fianchettoes solidly and castles kingside.

name: Polish Opening: Myers Variation
description: White advances queenside pawns with b4 and a4 while Black seizes the center with d5 and c6.

name: Polish Opening: Outflank Variation
description: Black responds to White's b4 with c6, preparing to advance d5 and establish central control.

name: Polish Opening: Outflank Variation, Schuehler Gambit
description: White sacrifices the b5 pawn attacking c6, while Black counters with a5 for queenside activity.

name: Polish Opening: Queenside Defense

name: Polish Opening: Queen's Indian Variation
description: Black mirrors White's queenside expansion with b6, creating a Queen's Indian structure from the Polish opening.

name: Polish Opening: Rooks Swap Line

name: Polish Opening: Schiffler-Sokolsky Variation
description: Black stakes a central d5 while White builds structure with e3, creating tension-filled strategic play.

name: Polish Opening: Schuehler Gambit
description: White sacrifices the b-pawn with b5 and follows e4 to seize the center after Black captures.

name: Polish Opening: Symmetrical Variation
description: Both sides mirror each other's queenside b-pawn advances, creating an unusual and highly symmetrical position.

name: Polish Opening: Tartakower Gambit
description: White launches e4 after Black's kingside f6, creating immediate central tension from an unconventional opening.

name: Polish Opening: Wolferts Gambit
description: Black strikes at both the center and queenside with e5 and c5, meeting White's unusual fianchetto setup.

name: Sodium Attack: Celadon Variation
description: Black captures White's misplaced knight, but White compensates with a3 and central structure (e3, d3).

name: Sodium Attack: Chenoboskion Variation

name: Sodium Attack: Durkin Gambit

name: Van Geet Opening: Damhaug Gambit

name: Van Geet Opening: Düsseldorf Gambit

description: White plays quiet moves (b3, e4, d3) while Black seizes space, sacrificing to White's emerging center.

name: Van Geet Opening: Jendrossek Gambit
description: White sacrifices the f-pawn with active knight maneuvers, while Black pushes in center and queenside.

name: Van Geet Opening: Kluever Gambit
description: White sacrifices e4 to open the center after Black's kingside f5; d3 maintains White's presence.

name: Van Geet Opening: Laroche Gambit

name: Van Geet Opening: Liebig Gambit
description: White places the queen aggressively on h5, while Black solidifies the center with e5 and d5.

name: Van Geet Opening: Melleby Gambit
description: White sacrifices the f-pawn, while Black responds with d4 and c5, seizing space from the setup.

name: Van Geet Opening: Myers Attack
description: White storms the kingside with h4 while Black fianchettoes with g6, creating immediate tactical pressure.

name: Van Geet Opening: Napoleon Attack

name: Van Geet Opening: Nowokunski Gambit

description: After 3.Ne4, White continues developing with 4.Nf3, supporting the center and adding piece activity. A modest positional approach to the gambit line.

name: Van Geet Opening: Reversed Nimzowitsch

name: Van Geet Opening: Reversed Scandinavian

name: Van Geet Opening: Sicilian Two Knights

name: Van Geet Opening: Sleipnir Gambit

name: Van Geet Opening: Tübingen Gambit
description: White plays the kingside-storming 2.g4, immediately seizing space and weakening the light squares around the king. A provocative and unsound aggressive try.

name: Van Geet Opening: Venezolana Variation
description: White adopts a quiet setup with 2.d3 and 3.g3, preparing a fianchetto structure and modest development. A restrained and positional approach.

name: Van Geet Opening: Warsteiner Gambit
description: White plays 2.f4 followed by Black's sharp 2...g5, offering immediate tactical clashes on the kingside. A wild, complications-seeking gambit.

name: Van't Kruijs Opening: Bouncing Bishop Variation

name: Van't Kruijs Opening: Keoni-Hiva Gambit, Akahi Variation
description: White sacrifices the f-pawn with 3.f4, inviting Black to capture while maintaining central control and developing the knight to f3. A pawn-offering setup.

name: Van't Kruijs Opening: Keoni-Hiva Gambit, Alua Variation

name: Van't Kruijs Opening: Keoni-Hiva Gambit, Ekolu Variation

name: Ware Opening: Cologne Gambit

name: Ware Opening: Crab Variation

name: Ware Opening: Meadow Hay Trap
description: White plays 2.Ra3, an unusual rook placement on the third rank. This eccentric setup offers no clear strategic purpose.

name: Ware Opening: Symmetric Variation

name: Ware Opening: Wing Gambit
description: White sacrifices the a-pawn with 2.axb5, allowing Black to develop with Bb7 and gain space. A queenside pawn-offering gambit.

name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack: Classical Variation

name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack: Dutch Variation

name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack: English Variation

name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack: Graz Attack
description: White develops the bishop to a3 after 1.b3, pinning Black's central d5-pawn and controlling key light squares. An aggressive pin-based setup.

name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack: Indian Variation
description: Black develops the knight to f6 in response to 1.b3, adopting a modest Indian-style setup. A solid developmental approach.

name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack: Modern Variation
description: White fianchettos the bishop on b2, plays c4 for central control, and develops a kingside-heavy setup with careful piece placement. A well-structured modern approach.

name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack: Pachman Gambit
description: White sacrifices the f-pawn with 3.f4 after fianchettoing, offering material for aggressive kingside attack. A sharp tactical gambit.

name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack: Polish Variation

name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack: Ringelbach Gambit
description: White plays 3.e4, striking at Black's f5 pawn and opening the center after Black has advanced kingside pawns. A central counter-gambit.

name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack: Spike Variation
description: After Black's fianchetto with g6, White launches a kingside pawn storm with 3.g4, attacking space aggressively. An unsound kingside assault.

name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack: Symmetrical Variation
description: Both sides fianchetto their kingside bishops after 1.b3 b6, establishing a symmetric and positional setup. A balanced hypermodern structure.

name: Bird Opening: Batavo-Polish Attack
description: After Black develops Nf6 and prepares a fianchetto with g6, White plays 3.b4, launching a queenside pawn attack. An unusual wing gambit.

name: Bird Opening: Double Duck Formation
description: Both sides mirror each other's f and d pawn advances (f4-f5, d4-d5), creating a symmetric pawn skeleton. A balanced classical structure.

name: Bird Opening: From's Gambit
description: White plays 1.f4, the Bird Opening, and Black immediately counterattacks with 1...e5. A direct challenge to White's kingside control.

name: Bird Opening: From's Gambit, Bahr Gambit
description: White develops Nc3 instead of capturing on e5, allowing Black to maintain central tension. A flexible knight-development approach to the gambit.

name: Bird Opening: From's Gambit, Langheld Gambit
description: White captures on e5 and again on d6, establishing a strong pawn on d6 while Black develops naturally with Nf6. White maintains a material advantage.

name: Bird Opening: From's Gambit, Lasker Variation
description: After Black recaptures on d6 with the bishop, Black launches a kingside counterattack with g5. A sharp, complications-rich variation.

name: Bird Opening: From's Gambit, Lipke Variation
description: White establishes a pawn on d4 after Black develops the knight to h6 and bishop to d6. White centralizes while Black's knight sits on the rim.

name: Bird Opening: Hobbs Gambit
description: Black immediately plays 1...g5, attacking White's f4 pawn and launching a bold kingside assault. A sharp, speculative counterattack.

name: Bird Opening: Hobbs-Zilbermints Gambit
description: Black first plays h6, then follows with g5, preparing a kingside pawn storm against White's opening move. A delayed but aggressive kingside attack.

name: Bird Opening: Horsefly Defense
description: Black develops the knight to h6, an unconventional and passive square that abandons central play. A slow, sideline defensive setup.

name: Bird Opening: Lasker Gambit
description: Black plays f6, attacking White's captured e5 pawn while preparing to recapture and open lines. A counterattacking gambit defense.

name: Bird Opening: Mujannah
description: White combines f4 with an immediate queenside expansion via c4, establishing control on both flanks. A broad opening strategy.

name: Bird Opening: Myers Defense
description: Black plays b5, launching an immediate queenside pawn attack against White's kingside-focused Bird Opening. A counterflank strategy.

name: Bird Opening: Platz Gambit
description: Black develops Ne7 after White captures on e5, positioning the knight for future f5 or g6 maneuvers. A flexible knight placement.

name: Bird Opening: Schlechter Gambit
description: Black develops the knight to c6 after e5 is captured, establishing central piece activity. A standard developmental response to the gambit.

name: Bird Opening: Siegener Gambit
description: White plays d4 (not fxe5), maintaining central tension; after exd4 and Nf3, White plays c3 to support a future pawn center. A flexible gambit approach.

name: Bird Opening: Swiss Gambit
description: White plays e4, challenging Black's f5 pawn, followed by a kingside pawn storm with g4. An aggressive central and flank combination.

name: Bird Opening: Wagner-Zwitersch Gambit
description: White plays e4, attacking Black's f5 pawn and opening the center after Black mirrors f4 with f5. A sharp central counter-gambit.

name: Bird Opening: Dutch Variation
description: White flank thrust with 1.f4, Black counters with central 1...d5 for early pawn contact.

name: Bird Opening: Dutch Variation, Dudweiler Gambit
description: White sacrifices the g-pawn with 2.g4 to open kingside lines after 1.f4 d5.

name: Bird Opening: Lasker Variation
description: After 1.f4 d5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.e3, Black strikes center with 3...c5, disrupting White's setup.

name: Bird Opening: Sturm Gambit
description: White supports the center with 2.c4 after 1.f4 d5, adopting a queen's gambit structure.

name: Bird Opening: Thomas Gambit
description: White fianchettoes with 2.b3 and Bb2, allowing Black's 3...d4 before pivoting with 5.e3.

name: Bird Opening: Williams Gambit
description: White sacrifices e4 to open central lines and mobilize pieces with Nc3 and Qe2.

name: Bird Opening: Williams-Zilbermints Gambit
description: White sacrifices e4 and activates both knights (Nc3, Nge2) for rapid attacking chances.

name: Colle System: Rhamphorhynchus Variation

name: Modern Defense: Semi-Averbakh Variation, Polish Variation
description: White builds strong center with e4 while Black fianchettoes kingside and pressures queenside with Qb6.

name: Modern Defense: Semi-Averbakh Variation, Pterodactyl Variation
description: Black fianchettoes and checks immediately with 4...Qa5+, forcing White's pieces into complications.

name: Modern Defense: Semi-Averbakh Variation, Pterodactyl Variation Accepted
description: White dominates center with d4, e4, c4; Black fianchettoes and maintains complex tension with checks.

name: Zukertort Defense: Kingside Variation

name: Zukertort Defense: Sicilian Knight Variation
description: Black develops a-knight early, then plays Sicilian 2...c5, challenging White's center from the flank.

name: Zukertort Opening: Arctic Defense

name: Zukertort Opening: Arctic Defense, Drunken Knight Variation
description: After 1...f6 and 2...Nh6, Black continues 3...Nf7 awkwardly while White seizes central space.

name: Zukertort Opening: Basman Defense
description: Black plays the oddball 1...h6, sidestep established theory while keeping all options maximally open.

name: Zukertort Opening: Black Mustang Defense
description: Black develops the c-knight immediately with 1...Nc6, a straightforward reply to White's setup.

name: Zukertort Opening: Drunken Cavalry Variation
description: Black develops both side knights unusually (1...Na6, 2...Nh6), adopting an eccentric flexible setup.

name: Zukertort Opening: Dutch Variation

name: Zukertort Opening: Herrstrom Gambit
description: Black immediately weakens the kingside with 1...g5, an ultra-aggressive and objectively dubious gambit.

name: Zukertort Opening: Kingside Fianchetto
description: Black fianchettoes kingside with 1...g6, building a solid hypermodern setup with long-diagonal control.

name: Zukertort Opening: Lisitsyn Gambit

name: Zukertort Opening: Lisitsyn Gambit Deferred
description: White delays the e4 push with 2.d3, playing 3.e4 gradually against Black's Dutch formation.

name: Zukertort Opening: Pirc Invitation
description: Black plays 1...d6, inviting a Pirc-like structure with flexible central tension.

name: Zukertort Opening: Polish Defense
description: Black immediately expands the queenside with 1...b5, a hypermodern flank push avoiding central contact.

name: Zukertort Opening: Queen's Gambit Invitation
description: Black plays 1...e6, inviting a Queen's Gambit structure while maintaining central flexibility.

name: Zukertort Opening: Queenside Fianchetto Variation
description: Black fianchettoes queenside with 1...b6, an unconventional setup giving the bishop a powerful diagonal.

name: Zukertort Opening: Ross Gambit
description: Black stakes the center immediately with 1...e5, a classical and aggressive response.

name: Zukertort Opening: Shabalov Gambit
description: Black challenges center with 3...c5 and expands queenside with 2...a6 and 4...b5 simultaneously.

name: Zukertort Opening: Sicilian Invitation
description: Black invites Sicilian-type play with 1...c5, attacking the center from the flank immediately.

name: Zukertort Opening: Slav Invitation
description: Black plays 1...c6, supporting a future d5 advance in Slav style while remaining flexible.

name: Zukertort Opening: Speelsmet Gambit
description: White sacrifices d4 with 2.d4 cxd4 3.e3, retaining central control and rapid piece activity.

name: Zukertort Opening: St. George Defense
